question.problem:
A function $f(x)$ has values according to the table below:

| $x$ | $2.4$ | $2.5$ | $2.6$ | $2.7$ | $2.8$ | $2.9$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $30$ | $28$ | $27$ | $25$ | $24$ | $22$ |

Approximate ${f}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=2.9$ using a backward difference approximation. Do not round the answer.

$\,\,{f}^{′}(2.9)≈$ {{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{f}^{′}(x)≈\frac{f(x)-f(x-h)}{h}
$$

 

at the point $x=2.9.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case, $h=0.1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(2.9) & ≈\frac{f(2.9)-f(2.9-0.1)}{0.1} \\  & =\frac{f(2.9)-f(2.8)}{0.1} \\  & =\frac{22-24}{0.1} \\  & =\frac{-2}{0.1} \\  & =-20.\end{aligned}
$$
